themes.theme: Pericarditis: วินิจฉัยจากท่าโน้มตัว + ECG ST ยกทุก lead / PR กด

items.q: A 35-year-old man has sharp retrosternal chest pain for 2 days that is worse when lying flat and on deep inspiration, and is relieved by sitting up and leaning forward. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Acute pericarditis

items.q: A patient with pleuritic chest pain relieved by sitting forward has an ECG showing widespread concave ST elevation with PR depression, and a scratchy triphasic sound at the left lower sternal border. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Acute pericarditis

items.q: An ECG shows ST elevation in all leads except aVR, where there is ST depression with PR elevation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Acute pericarditis

items.q: A young man has chest pain and an ECG with widespread ST elevation. Troponin-I is markedly elevated but coronary angiography shows normal coronary arteries and echocardiography shows mildly reduced left ventricular function. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Myopericarditis

items.q: Which ECG pattern is most characteristic of acute pericarditis rather than myocardial infarction?
items.a: Widespread concave ST elevation with PR depression and no reciprocal change

themes.theme: Pericarditis: รักษาด้วย NSAID/aspirin + colchicine

items.q: A 38-year-old man with acute pericarditis after a viral illness has no effusion and normal cardiac function. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
items.a: High-dose aspirin or an NSAID plus colchicine

items.q: A patient with acute pericarditis has pleuritic chest pain relieved by leaning forward. Which drug combination is first-line?
items.a: Aspirin or an NSAID plus colchicine

themes.theme: Cardiac tamponade: Beck triad, pulsus paradoxus, electrical alternans → pericardiocentesis

items.q: An ECG shows beat-to-beat variation in the amplitude of the QRS complexes (electrical alternans) with sinus tachycardia and low voltage. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Cardiac tamponade

items.q: A hypotensive patient has an ECG with low voltage and electrical alternans, and echocardiography shows a large pericardial effusion with right atrial collapse. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
items.a: Urgent echo-guided pericardiocentesis

items.q: A patient with known pericardial effusion becomes hypotensive with BP 80/50 mmHg, pulse 120/min, and distended neck veins that do not collapse on inspiration. Which physical sign best supports tamponade physiology?
items.a: Pulsus paradoxus — an inspiratory fall in systolic pressure of more than 10 mmHg

items.q: In cardiac tamponade, echocardiography shows right atrial and right ventricular diastolic collapse. Which mechanism best explains the haemodynamic compromise?
items.a: Raised intrapericardial pressure impairs diastolic filling, with ventricular interdependence across the septum

items.q: A 40-year-old woman with breast cancer treated with a CAF regimen 6 months ago presents with dyspnoea, BP 80/60 mmHg, JVP elevated 10 cm, clear lungs and cardiomegaly on chest radiograph. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Pericardial effusion with tamponade

items.q: A dyspnoeic patient has a chest radiograph showing an enlarged globular 'water-bottle' cardiac silhouette with clear lung fields. What is the most appropriate next step?
items.a: Echocardiography, and pericardiocentesis if there is tamponade physiology

themes.theme: Constrictive pericarditis ต่างจาก tamponade

items.q: Which physical finding is characteristic of constrictive pericarditis rather than cardiac tamponade?
items.a: Pericardial knock with Kussmaul sign and a prominent y descent

themes.theme: Pericardial effusion: TB (ADA สูง) vs มะเร็ง

items.q: Which finding on pericardial fluid analysis most suggests a tuberculous rather than a malignant pericardial effusion?
items.a: Lymphocyte-predominant exudate with high adenosine deaminase

themes.theme: Myocarditis: สาเหตุส่วนใหญ่คือไวรัส

items.q: What is the most common cause of myocarditis in previously healthy adults?
items.a: Viral infection

themes.theme: Doxorubicin cardiomyopathy

items.q: Which chemotherapeutic agent is most characteristically associated with dose-dependent cardiomyopathy?
items.a: Doxorubicin

themes.theme: ECG บอกตำแหน่ง STEMI (ผนัง/หลอดเลือด, right-sided lead)

items.q: A patient with a pleural effusion has an ECG showing ST elevation in leads V1 to V4 with reciprocal ST depression inferiorly and elevated troponin. What is the most likely cause of the ECG change?
items.a: Anterior wall myocardial infarction

items.q: An ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF. Which additional leads should be recorded?
items.a: Right-sided leads V3R and V4R

items.q: ST elevation in leads V1 to V4 corresponds to infarction of which wall and which artery?
items.a: Anterior wall — left anterior descending artery

items.q: A 60-year-old woman with diabetes, dyslipidaemia and known coronary disease has 10 minutes of chest tightness. ECG shows ST elevation in I, aVL and V2-V6 with reciprocal depression in II, III and aVF, and troponin-I is 8 ng/mL. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Acute anterolateral ST-elevation myocardial infarction

items.q: An ECG shows ST elevation in II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL, rate 75/min, sinus rhythm and narrow QRS. What is the complete interpretation?
items.a: Normal sinus rhythm with acute inferior wall ST-elevation myocardial infarction

items.q: An ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL in a patient with 2 hours of chest pain. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Acute inferior wall myocardial infarction

themes.theme: จำแนกชนิด shock และ hemodynamics (JVP, SVR)

items.q: A patient has muffled heart sounds, hypotension and distended neck veins, then develops shock. What type of shock is this?
items.a: Obstructive shock

items.q: Cardiac tamponade causes which category of shock?
items.a: Obstructive shock

items.q: A patient admitted with pneumonia develops fever 39 C, BP 80/45 mmHg, warm extremities and bounding pulses 2 days after starting antibiotics. What type of shock is most likely?
items.a: Septic (distributive) shock

items.q: A patient with cardiomegaly presents with shock, heart rate 130/min and an irregularly irregular pulse, with crepitations at both lung bases and cold extremities. What type of shock is this?
items.a: Cardiogenic shock

items.q: Anaphylactic shock belongs to which category of shock?
items.a: Distributive shock

items.q: Which bedside finding best distinguishes hypovolaemic shock from cardiogenic and obstructive shock?
items.a: Flat (low) jugular venous pressure

items.q: Which haemodynamic pattern fits distributive (septic) shock before fluid resuscitation?
items.a: Low systemic vascular resistance with high or normal cardiac output

themes.theme: Tachyarrhythmia ไม่เสถียร → synchronized cardioversion / defibrillation

items.q: A hypotensive patient has an irregularly irregular tachycardia at 150/min, elevated JVP and cold clammy skin. Which is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
items.a: Synchronised cardioversion

items.q: A patient with palpitations and dyspnoea has no palpable pulse but is conscious and talking. The monitor shows atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. What should be done?
items.a: Recheck the pulse and monitor leads; if the patient is unstable, perform synchronised cardioversion

items.q: A patient with monomorphic ventricular tachycardia at 180/min has BP 78/40 mmHg, chest pain and is drowsy but has a pulse. What is the immediate treatment?
items.a: Synchronised cardioversion

items.q: A monitored patient in the ICU suddenly becomes pulseless with ventricular tachycardia on the monitor. What is the best first therapy?
items.a: Immediate unsynchronised defibrillation

themes.theme: AF กับ stroke: CHA2DS2-VASc, MS + AF → warfarin

items.q: A 72-year-old man with atrial fibrillation at 130/min develops acute hemiparesis and hypotension. What is the most likely mechanism of the neurological event?
items.a: Cardioembolism from the left atrium

items.q: Which score should be used to decide on anticoagulation for stroke prevention in non-valvular atrial fibrillation?
items.a: CHA2DS2-VASc score

items.q: A patient with rheumatic mitral stenosis and atrial fibrillation develops sudden right hemiparesis. Which anticoagulant is indicated?
items.a: Warfarin with INR 2 to 3

items.q: A patient with atrial flutter develops an embolic stroke. What is the underlying mechanism?
items.a: Thrombus formation in the fibrillating/fluttering atrium with embolisation

themes.theme: Anaphylaxis: type I, IM adrenaline, พก auto-injector

items.q: A woman develops generalised urticaria, wheeze and BP 80/50 mmHg minutes after dinner. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
items.a: Intramuscular adrenaline into the anterolateral thigh

items.q: Urticaria and anaphylaxis are which type of hypersensitivity reaction?
items.a: Type I (IgE-mediated)

items.q: A patient who survived anaphylactic shock is being discharged. What is the most important item to provide?
items.a: An adrenaline auto-injector with training and a written action plan

items.q: A 32-year-old man develops generalized itchy wheals within 30 minutes of taking an oral antibiotic. The lesions blanch on pressure and each individual wheal disappears within a few hours. Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is this?
items.a: Type I (IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity)

items.q: A patient who survived anaphylactic shock from a bee sting is being discharged. Which of the following is the most appropriate advice?
items.a: Carry an adrenaline auto-injector at all times and use it immediately when symptoms begin

items.q: A 28-year-old woman develops itching, generalized flushing, wheezing and hypotension 15 minutes after eating at a restaurant. Which is the most appropriate first drug and route?
items.a: Adrenaline 0.3-0.5 mg intramuscularly

themes.theme: ขาดน้ำ/shock ± Na ต่ำ → 0.9% NSS

items.q: A hypotensive patient has flat neck veins, dry mucous membranes, poor skin turgor and a history of profuse diarrhoea. What is the most appropriate initial management?
items.a: Rapid infusion of isotonic crystalloid (0.9% normal saline)

items.q: A patient with severe vomiting and diarrhoea has BP 85/50 mmHg, Na 120 mEq/L, BUN 40 mg/dL and creatinine 1.8 mg/dL. What is the most appropriate initial fluid?
items.a: 0.9% normal saline

items.q: A patient with vomiting for 3 days has Na 105 mEq/L, dry mucous membranes, flat neck veins and BP 90/60 mmHg without seizure or coma. What fluid should be given?
items.a: 0.9% normal saline

items.q: A patient with hypovolaemic shock has Na 112 mEq/L with elevated BUN and creatinine. What is the initial treatment?
items.a: Isotonic saline resuscitation with frequent monitoring of serum sodium

items.q: A dehydrated patient has Na 122 mEq/L and K 5.8 mEq/L with postural hypotension. What is the most appropriate initial fluid?
items.a: 0.9% normal saline

themes.theme: Vasovagal ระหว่างเจาะน้ำในช่องปอด

items.q: During thoracentesis a patient becomes light-headed with cold extremities. BP 80/60 mmHg, pulse 40/min, and breath sounds are equal bilaterally. What is the most likely cause?
items.a: Vasovagal reaction

items.q: During thoracentesis a patient becomes light-headed with cold extremities. Blood pressure is 80/60 mmHg and pulse rate 40/min. Breath sounds are equal on both sides. What is the most likely cause?
items.a: Vasovagal reaction

themes.theme: Shock liver (ischemic hepatitis)

items.q: A patient in prolonged shock is found to have AST 1,800 U/L and ALT 1,600 U/L with normal alkaline phosphatase, which fall rapidly over 3 days after blood pressure is restored. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Ischaemic hepatitis (shock liver)

themes.theme: STEMI reperfusion: primary PCI vs fibrinolysis, เกณฑ์สำเร็จ

items.q: A patient with ST elevation in V1-V4 and elevated troponin-T can reach a PCI-capable centre within 120 minutes of first medical contact. What is the most appropriate reperfusion strategy?
items.a: Transfer for primary percutaneous coronary intervention

items.q: A patient with acute coronary syndrome has been given aspirin, a P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulant, statin and nitrate. What is the definitive next step in STEMI?
items.a: Reperfusion therapy — primary PCI or fibrinolysis

items.q: A patient with an anterolateral STEMI is treated with fibrinolysis. Which finding best indicates successful reperfusion at 90 minutes?
items.a: Resolution of ST elevation by more than 50 percent with relief of chest pain

items.q: Why is primary PCI preferred over fibrinolysis when both are available within the recommended time?
items.a: It achieves higher rates of vessel patency with lower rates of reinfarction and intracranial haemorrhage

themes.theme: กลไก ischemia: plaque rupture, fixed stenosis, microvascular

items.q: What is the most common underlying mechanism of ST-elevation myocardial infarction?
items.a: Rupture or erosion of an atherosclerotic plaque with superimposed thrombus

items.q: What is the mechanism of chest pain that occurs on exertion and resolves with rest in stable coronary disease?
items.a: A fixed atherosclerotic stenosis limits flow so supply cannot meet the increased myocardial oxygen demand

items.q: A patient with typical angina has normal epicardial coronary arteries on angiography. What is the most likely explanation?
items.a: Coronary microvascular dysfunction with supply-demand mismatch

themes.theme: ACS spectrum: stable angina / UA / NSTEMI, troponin ซ้ำ, high-risk

items.q: Which chest pain pattern is most consistent with acute coronary syndrome?
items.a: Pain at rest or with a crescendo pattern, radiating to the jaw or arm, with diaphoresis

items.q: A patient has typical chest pain at rest for 20 minutes with dyspnoea. ECG shows no ST elevation and troponin is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Unstable angina

items.q: A 58-year-old man has retrosternal tightness on exertion for 3 months that resolves within 5 minutes of rest. ECG, troponin and chest radiograph at rest are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Stable (typical) angina pectoris

items.q: A patient with ongoing chest pain has a normal ECG and normal initial troponin-I taken 1 hour after pain onset. What is the most appropriate next step?
items.a: Repeat ECG and troponin serially over the next few hours

items.q: Which feature identifies a high-risk non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome requiring early invasive strategy within 24 hours?
items.a: Rising troponin with dynamic ST-T changes or a GRACE score above 140

themes.theme: Mechanical complication หลัง MI (VSR)

items.q: Three days after an inferior STEMI a patient develops acute dyspnoea, hypotension and a new loud pansystolic murmur with a thrill at the lower sternal border. What is the most likely complication?
items.a: Mechanical complication — ventricular septal rupture or acute mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture

items.q: Three days after an acute myocardial infarction a patient develops a new pansystolic murmur at the lower left sternal border with a thrill and acute pulmonary oedema. What is the most likely cause?
items.a: Ventricular septal rupture

themes.theme: ไขมัน/statin/FH

items.q: Which patient has the clearest indication for high-intensity statin therapy?
items.a: A 60-year-old man 2 weeks after an acute ischaemic stroke of atherosclerotic origin

items.q: A 35-year-old man whose father died of myocardial infarction at 40 has LDL 260 mg/dL, tendon xanthomata at the Achilles tendon and corneal arcus. Which defect is most likely?
items.a: Defective LDL receptor function

items.q: A 28-year-old asymptomatic man has a strong family history of premature coronary disease. Which investigation is most appropriate first?
items.a: Fasting lipid profile

themes.theme: เจ็บแน่นหน้าอก → ตรวจแรกคือ ECG 12 lead

items.q: A patient presents with exertional dyspnoea and chest discomfort. What is the most appropriate first investigation?
items.a: 12-lead electrocardiogram

themes.theme: Stable angina: ห้าม short-acting nifedipine

items.q: Which statement about the management of chronic stable angina is correct?
items.a: Short-acting nifedipine should not be used because reflex tachycardia may worsen ischaemia

themes.theme: ลำดับการอ่าน/รายงาน ECG

items.q: When reading a 12-lead ECG of suspected STEMI, which sequence should be described?
items.a: Rate, rhythm, axis, intervals, chamber enlargement, ST-T changes and Q waves

items.q: When describing an ECG in a SAQ station, which set of elements must be reported?
items.a: Rate, rhythm, axis, intervals, chamber enlargement, ST-T changes and Q waves

themes.theme: Secondary prevention หลัง MI

items.q: After reperfusion, which combination is standard long-term secondary prevention following myocardial infarction?
items.a: Dual antiplatelet therapy, high-intensity statin, beta-blocker and ACE inhibitor with risk-factor control

themes.theme: ยาคุม rate/rhythm ของ AF

items.q: A 70-year-old man with atrial fibrillation at 140/min, stable blood pressure and no heart failure needs rate control. Which drug is most appropriate first?
items.a: A beta-blocker such as metoprolol (or a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker)

items.q: Which drug controls symptoms of atrial fibrillation by controlling rate or rhythm rather than preventing stroke?
items.a: Atenolol or amiodarone

themes.theme: จำ AF ให้ได้: pulse deficit, ECG, RVR → HF/syncope

items.q: What is the characteristic physical finding of atrial fibrillation?
items.a: An irregularly irregular pulse with a pulse deficit

items.q: A patient with known heart failure develops palpitations with an irregular tachycardia at 150/min and worsening dyspnoea. What is the most likely arrhythmia?
items.a: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

items.q: An 80-year-old man has palpitations followed by transient loss of consciousness. BP 140/90 mmHg, pulse irregular 110-160/min. What is the most likely cause of the syncope?
items.a: Reduced cardiac output from the rapid irregular ventricular rate

items.q: An ECG shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with absent P waves and a ventricular rate of 130/min. What is the interpretation?
items.a: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

themes.theme: Bradyarrhythmia: AV block ทุกดีกรี, SSS → pacing

items.q: An elderly patient with tachy-brady syndrome has an irregularly irregular pulse alternating with pauses and dizziness. What is the underlying problem?
items.a: Sick sinus syndrome with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation

items.q: An ECG shows a constant PR interval of 0.26 seconds with every P wave followed by a QRS complex. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: First-degree atrioventricular block

items.q: An asymptomatic 45-year-old man has first-degree AV block on a routine ECG with normal examination. What is the appropriate management?
items.a: Observation with review of AV-nodal blocking drugs

items.q: An ECG shows progressive PR prolongation until a P wave is not conducted, then the cycle repeats. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Second-degree AV block Mobitz type I (Wenckebach)

items.q: An ECG shows intermittently dropped QRS complexes with a constant PR interval in the conducted beats and a wide QRS. What is the diagnosis and management?
items.a: Mobitz type II block — permanent pacemaker

items.q: An ECG shows P waves and QRS complexes that are completely dissociated, with a ventricular rate of 35/min and a wide QRS. The patient is dizzy with BP 85/50 mmHg. What is the definitive treatment?
items.a: Temporary pacing followed by a permanent pacemaker

themes.theme: ต้นเหตุ tachyarrhythmia: thyrotoxicosis / thyroid storm / alcohol

items.q: A 45-year-old man has palpitations every Monday after weekend drinking. ECG during symptoms shows atrial fibrillation that terminates spontaneously. What is the most likely precipitant?
items.a: Alcohol (holiday heart syndrome)

items.q: Untreated hyperthyroidism most characteristically precipitates which arrhythmia?
items.a: Atrial fibrillation

items.q: A patient has fever 39 C, heart failure, atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, agitation and suppressed TSH with high free T4. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Thyroid storm

items.q: A patient presents with palpitations and an otherwise normal examination. Which two investigations are most appropriate first?
items.a: 12-lead ECG and thyroid function test

items.q: An ECG shows sinus tachycardia in a patient with weight loss, tremor and heat intolerance. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Thyrotoxicosis

themes.theme: SVT → adenosine

items.q: A stable patient has a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 180/min with no visible P waves. Vagal manoeuvres fail. What is the next step?
items.a: Intravenous adenosine 6 mg rapid push

themes.theme: HyperK: ECG T สูงแหลม → Ca gluconate, ยาลด K

items.q: An ECG shows tall peaked T waves with a widened QRS in a patient with chronic kidney disease. What is the first drug to give?
items.a: Intravenous calcium gluconate

items.q: A patient with CKD on two nephrotoxic drugs has an ECG showing tall peaked T waves, rate 120/min, sinus rhythm, P waves present and a narrow QRS. What is the interpretation?
items.a: Sinus tachycardia with ECG changes of hyperkalaemia

items.q: An ECG shows tall peaked T waves in a patient who is drowsy with muscle weakness. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Hyperkalaemia

items.q: An ECG shows tall peaked T waves in a patient with CKD. What is the first drug to give and why?
items.a: Intravenous calcium gluconate to stabilise the cardiac membrane

items.q: Which drug does NOT lower serum potassium?
items.a: Spironolactone

items.q: A CKD patient on two nephrotoxic drugs has an ECG showing tall peaked T waves with sinus tachycardia and narrow QRS. What is the interpretation and immediate treatment?
items.a: Hyperkalaemia — give intravenous calcium gluconate then insulin with dextrose

themes.theme: Mitral stenosis: เสียง, rheumatic, echo

items.q: Which physical finding is consistent with mitral stenosis?
items.a: An opening snap followed by a diastolic rumbling murmur at the apex

items.q: Which finding is NOT a sign of mitral stenosis?
items.a: Systolic ejection murmur at the right upper parasternal border

items.q: A patient has a low-pitched diastolic rumbling murmur heard best at the apex in the left lateral decubitus position, with a loud S1. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Mitral stenosis

items.q: Echocardiography in a patient with a murmur shows a thickened mitral valve with restricted opening and a mean gradient of 12 mmHg. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Significant mitral stenosis

items.q: A 40-year-old woman has 1 month of exertional dyspnoea and orthopnoea, an irregularly irregular pulse, a loud S1 with an opening snap and a diastolic rumble at the apex. What is the most likely complete diagnosis?
items.a: Rheumatic mitral stenosis with atrial fibrillation and heart failure

items.q: Which valve lesion is the most common long-term sequela of acute rheumatic fever in Thailand?
items.a: Mitral stenosis

themes.theme: Aortic regurgitation (รวม Marfan)

items.q: A patient has a wide pulse pressure with a high-pitched blowing decrescendo diastolic murmur at the left sternal border. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Aortic regurgitation

items.q: A tall thin 19-year-old woman with long arms and arachnodactyly has BP 180/70 mmHg, a bounding pulse and a high-pitched blowing decrescendo diastolic murmur. What is the most likely underlying condition?
items.a: Aortic regurgitation from aortic root dilatation in Marfan syndrome

themes.theme: Aortic stenosis

items.q: A systolic ejection murmur at the right upper sternal border radiating to the carotids with a slow-rising pulse indicates which lesion?
items.a: Aortic stenosis

items.q: Which finding is NOT expected in severe aortic stenosis?
items.a: Wide pulse pressure with a collapsing pulse

themes.theme: MR / MVP

items.q: A patient has a pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla, with bilateral leg oedema and lung crepitations. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Mitral regurgitation with congestive heart failure

items.q: A young woman has a mid-systolic click followed by a late systolic murmur that moves earlier on standing. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Mitral valve prolapse

themes.theme: Congenital shunt murmur (PDA / ASD)

items.q: A continuous machinery murmur heard below the left clavicle in a young adult suggests which lesion?
items.a: Patent ductus arteriosus

items.q: A patient has right atrial and right ventricular enlargement with a fixed widely split S2 and a systolic murmur at the left upper sternal border. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Atrial septal defect

themes.theme: Pulmonary hypertension + right HF

items.q: A patient has a loud P2, elevated JVP, hepatomegaly and leg oedema with clear lungs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Pulmonary hypertension with right heart failure

themes.theme: Acute rheumatic fever (ASO, Jones)

items.q: A 12-year-old has migratory polyarthritis, a new murmur and fever 3 weeks after pharyngitis. Which investigation supports the diagnosis?
items.a: Anti-streptolysin O titre

items.q: Which skin finding is a major manifestation of acute rheumatic fever?
items.a: Erythema marginatum

themes.theme: Infective endocarditis: hemoculture, signs, ยา, prophylaxis

items.q: A patient has a murmur, leg oedema, fever for 3 weeks and splenomegaly. Which diagnosis should be excluded first?
items.a: Infective endocarditis

items.q: A 54-year-old man has fever for 3 months, splinter haemorrhages, conjunctival haemorrhage, a diastolic murmur of aortic regurgitation, and an oscillating mass on the aortic valve. Four sets of blood cultures grow viridans streptococci. What is the appropriate treatment?
items.a: Intravenous penicillin G for 4 weeks, or penicillin G plus gentamicin for 2 weeks

items.q: In infective endocarditis, what is a Roth spot?
items.a: A retinal haemorrhage with a pale centre

items.q: A patient with a prosthetic heart valve and penicillin allergy is scheduled for a dental extraction involving gingival manipulation. What is the most appropriate prophylaxis?
items.a: A single dose of clindamycin or azithromycin before the procedure

items.q: Which investigation is essential for diagnosing infective endocarditis?
items.a: At least three sets of blood cultures from different sites before antibiotics

themes.theme: วินิจฉัย HT: white coat / resistant / secondary / lifestyle

items.q: A patient has blood pressure 150/80 mmHg at the clinic but 120/80 mmHg on repeated home readings. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: White coat hypertension

items.q: A patient taking three antihypertensive drugs including a thiazide diuretic at optimal doses has BP 180/120 mmHg both at the clinic and at home. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Resistant hypertension

items.q: Which feature most suggests secondary rather than primary hypertension?
items.a: Sudden onset of severe hypertension in a young patient

items.q: Which lifestyle measure has the LEAST effect on lowering blood pressure?
items.a: A high-protein diet

themes.theme: เลือกยาลดความดันตามสถานการณ์ (RAS, ตั้งครรภ์, CCB บวม, dissection)

items.q: Which antihypertensive should be avoided in bilateral renal artery stenosis?
items.a: Enalapril (ACE inhibitor)

items.q: Which drug is most appropriate for chronic hypertension in pregnancy?
items.a: Methyldopa (or labetalol, nifedipine)

items.q: A hypertensive patient on amlodipine develops bilateral ankle oedema with a normal JVP, normal echocardiogram and no proteinuria. What is the most appropriate action?
items.a: Reduce or stop amlodipine and switch to or add an ACE inhibitor/ARB

items.q: In acute aortic dissection with BP 180/120 mmHg, which drug must NOT be given alone?
items.a: A direct vasodilator such as nitroprusside or hydralazine without a beta-blocker

themes.theme: HFrEF: GDMT (ACEI/ARNI + BB …)

items.q: Which antihypertensive class improves survival in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction?
items.a: ACE inhibitor such as enalapril

items.q: A patient with LVEF 30 percent and NYHA class II symptoms is on furosemide only. What should be added first?
items.a: An ACE inhibitor (or ARNI) plus a beta-blocker, then an MRA and SGLT2 inhibitor

themes.theme: Acute LHF / pulmonary edema: อาการ กลไก CXR

items.q: A patient wakes at night breathless and coughs pink frothy sputum, with orthopnoea and bibasal crepitations. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Acute left-sided heart failure with pulmonary oedema

items.q: What lung finding is typical of left-sided heart failure?
items.a: Bibasal fine inspiratory crepitations

items.q: What is the mechanism of pulmonary oedema in acute decompensated heart failure?
items.a: Raised pulmonary capillary hydrostatic pressure exceeding plasma oncotic pressure

items.q: Which chest radiographic features indicate congestive heart failure?
items.a: Cardiomegaly with upper lobe blood diversion, Kerley B lines and pleural effusion

themes.theme: HF พื้นฐาน: NYHA, precipitant, JVP แยกจากตับแข็ง

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a typical acute precipitant of decompensated heart failure?
items.a: Obesity

items.q: A patient is comfortable at rest but becomes breathless on ordinary activity such as walking on level ground. What is the NYHA functional class?
items.a: Class II

items.q: Which finding best distinguishes congestive heart failure from chronic liver disease as the cause of oedema and ascites?
items.a: Elevated jugular venous pressure

themes.theme: Cardiorenal / high-output state

items.q: A patient with heart failure has worsening congestion and a rising creatinine. What is the most appropriate management of type 1 cardiorenal syndrome?
items.a: Continue decongestion with intravenous loop diuretic and salt restriction, monitoring renal function

items.q: A patient has warm hands and feet, wide pulse pressure, rising creatinine and a preserved ejection fraction with high cardiac output. Which mechanism best explains the picture?
items.a: A high-output state with systemic vasodilatation and inadequate effective organ perfusion

items.q: A patient with heart failure and CKD has worsening congestion with rising creatinine. What is the appropriate approach?
items.a: Salt restriction with intravenous loop diuretic to achieve decongestion, and dialysis if diuretic-resistant

items.q: A patient with warm extremities, wide pulse pressure, rising creatinine and preserved ejection fraction most likely has which problem?
items.a: Inadequate effective organ perfusion in a high-output vasodilated state (e.g. sepsis, cirrhosis)

items.q: In cardiorenal syndrome type 1, which factor most drives the fall in renal function?
items.a: Venous congestion with raised central venous pressure

themes.theme: COPD hypercapnic respiratory failure: O2 เกิน, NIV

items.q: A 45-year-old smoker has dyspnoea with PaCO2 56 mmHg, pH 7.28 and severe airflow obstruction on spirometry, with clear lungs on radiograph and normal BNP. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Acute exacerbation of COPD with hypercapnic respiratory failure

items.q: A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department confused and drowsy. Arterial blood gas: PaO2 170 mmHg (on supplemental oxygen), PaCO2 56 mmHg, pH 7.28. He has a 15 pack-year smoking history and pulmonary function testing 3 months ago showed severe airway obstruction. What is the most likely cause of his hypercapnic respiratory failure?
items.a: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with excessive oxygen administration

items.q: A patient with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease has persistent dyspnoea and SpO2 88 percent despite oxygen by nasal cannula. ABG shows pH 7.28, PaCO2 65 mmHg and HCO3 28 mEq/L. He is alert and able to protect his airway. What is the most appropriate next step?
items.a: Non-invasive positive pressure ventilation

themes.theme: Diabetic nephropathy: hyperfiltration, UACR, SGLT2i, ACEI

items.q: A 60-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and dyslipidaemia on glibenclamide, enalapril and simvastatin has urine protein 2+ and creatinine 1.6 mg/dL. What is the most appropriate management?
items.a: Continue the ACE inhibitor for renoprotection, optimise glucose and blood pressure control, and add an SGLT2 inhibitor

items.q: Which factor most accelerates progression of chronic kidney disease in a diabetic patient with HbA1c 11 percent and albuminuria?
items.a: Poor glycaemic control with persistent albuminuria and uncontrolled blood pressure

items.q: What is the earliest pathophysiological change in diabetic nephropathy?
items.a: Glomerular hyperfiltration with intraglomerular hypertension

items.q: Which test is used to screen for and predict progression of diabetic nephropathy?
items.a: Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio

items.q: Which antidiabetic drug class has proven renoprotective benefit in patients with albuminuria?
items.a: SGLT2 inhibitor

themes.theme: ผลข้างเคียงยา TB (INH, RIF, PZA, EMB)

items.q: A 30-year-old previously healthy woman with smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis was started on isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol once daily. After 1 week she develops progressive nausea, vomiting and malaise. Physical findings are unremarkable. Liver function tests: total bilirubin / direct bilirubin 2.8 / 1.6 mg/dL, AST/ALT 180/170 U/L, ALP 150 U/L (normal <115). What is the most appropriate immediate management?
items.a: Stop all hepatotoxic drugs, switch to ethambutol plus a fluoroquinolone, then perform a drug challenge test when liver function recovers

items.q: A patient receiving the 2HRZE/4HR anti-tuberculous regimen develops painless blurring of vision in both eyes with impaired colour discrimination after several weeks of treatment. There is no eye redness or pain. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?
items.a: Stop ethambutol and refer to an ophthalmologist

items.q: Which anti-tuberculous drug most characteristically causes hyperuricaemia and may precipitate an acute gouty attack?
items.a: Pyrazinamide

items.q: A patient completing anti-tuberculous therapy notices that his urine, tears and sweat have turned orange-red. He feels well and liver function tests are normal. Which drug is responsible?
items.a: Rifampicin

items.q: Which anti-tuberculous drug causes peripheral neuropathy, and what is given to prevent it?
items.a: Isoniazid; prevented by pyridoxine (vitamin B6)

items.q: A patient on anti-tuberculous therapy develops joint pain with a serum uric acid of 10 mg/dL. Which drug is responsible?
items.a: Pyrazinamide

themes.theme: TB: วินิจฉัย/โปรแกรม (culture, MDR, adherence, isolation, apex)

items.q: What is the definition of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB)?
items.a: Resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin

items.q: A patient with smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis has been on the standard regimen for 8 weeks but his sputum smear remains AFB positive and his symptoms have not improved. He obtains his medication from the local health centre and admits missing doses frequently. Which is the most likely explanation and the best next step?
items.a: Poor adherence; assess and reinforce adherence with directly observed therapy while sending sputum for culture and drug susceptibility testing

items.q: A patient with newly diagnosed smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted. Which admission arrangement is most appropriate?
items.a: Admit to a negative-pressure isolation room and have all staff wear an N95 respirator

items.q: Which investigation is the gold standard for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis?
items.a: Mycobacterial culture of sputum

items.q: Reactivation pulmonary tuberculosis in an immunocompetent adult most characteristically involves which part of the lung, and why?
items.a: Apical and posterior segments of the upper lobes, because of the higher oxygen tension there

themes.theme: PCP ใน HIV / ผู้ได้ยากดภูมิ

items.q: A 34-year-old man with HIV infection who has never received antiretroviral therapy presents with 3 weeks of dry cough and progressive exertional dyspnoea. CD4 count is 125 cells/microlitre. Chest radiograph shows bilateral perihilar ground-glass opacities. Which organism is most likely responsible?
items.a: Pneumocystis jirovecii

items.q: A 36-year-old woman with HIV infection presents with 2 weeks of progressive exertional dyspnoea, low-grade fever and dry cough. Examination: BT 38 C, PR 130/min, RR 30/min, mild pallor, oral hairy leukoplakia, normal breath sounds with no adventitious sounds. ABG on room air: pH 7.45, PaO2 55 mmHg, PaCO2 30 mmHg, O2 saturation 80 percent. Apart from oxygen therapy, which treatment is most appropriate?
items.a: Cotrimoxazole plus systemic corticosteroid

items.q: A patient with SLE on prednisolone and immunosuppressants presents with 1 week of dry cough, fever and dyspnea with bilateral interstitial infiltrates and marked hypoxemia but an unremarkable lung examination. What should be done first?
items.a: Treat empirically for Pneumocystis pneumonia while investigating for infection

themes.theme: Drug-induced AIN (sterile pyuria, WBC cast)

items.q: A patient with pulmonary tuberculosis develops acute kidney injury 10 days after starting the standard four-drug regimen. Which urinary finding would best support drug-induced acute interstitial nephritis as the cause?
items.a: Sterile pyuria with white blood cell casts

items.q: A patient with minimal change disease on high-dose prednisolone develops acute kidney injury 2 weeks later with sterile pyuria and WBC casts. What is the most likely cause?
items.a: Acute interstitial nephritis from a concurrent drug

items.q: Which additional renal complication can NSAIDs cause besides reduced glomerular filtration?
items.a: Acute interstitial nephritis with or without minimal change disease

items.q: A patient on high-dose steroid for minimal change disease develops acute kidney injury with sterile pyuria, WBC casts, rash and eosinophilia after starting a new antibiotic. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Acute interstitial nephritis

themes.theme: อ่าน ABG

items.q: An arterial blood gas shows pH 7.15, PaCO2 30 mmHg and HCO3 10 mEq/L. Which acid-base disorder is present?
items.a: Mixed metabolic acidosis and respiratory acidosis

items.q: A patient becomes dyspnoeic 6 hours ago. Arterial blood gas on room air: pH 7.26, PaCO2 60 mmHg, HCO3 26 mEq/L, O2 saturation 80 percent. Which interpretation is correct?
items.a: Acute respiratory acidosis with minimal metabolic compensation

items.q: A 60-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents with worsening dyspnoea. Arterial blood gas: pH 7.30, PaCO2 80 mmHg, HCO3 38 mEq/L. Which interpretation is correct?
items.a: Acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis with partial metabolic compensation

items.q: A 56-year-old diabetic man presents with fever, productive cough and vomiting for 3 days. Vital signs: BT 38.5 C, PR 110/min, RR 28/min, BP 95/55 mmHg, moderate dehydration, crepitations at the lower lung. Laboratory results: blood sugar 128 mg/dL, BUN 14, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, Na 140, K 4.1, Cl 78, HCO3 15 mEq/L, albumin 4.0 g/dL. ABG: pH 7.50, PaO2 70 mmHg, PaCO2 20 mmHg. What best describes the acid-base abnormality?
items.a: Respiratory alkalosis from pneumonia, metabolic alkalosis from vomiting and high anion gap metabolic acidosis from lactic acidosis

items.q: A patient with diabetic ketoacidosis has an arterial blood gas showing pH 7.26, PaCO2 23 mmHg and HCO3 10 mEq/L, with Na 140, Cl 100 mEq/L. Which interpretation is correct?
items.a: High anion gap metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation

themes.theme: Hypoxemia physiology: shunt, A-a gradient, ARDS

items.q: Which statement correctly describes a physiological shunt?
items.a: Alveolar units that are perfused but not ventilated, causing hypoxaemia that does not correct with supplemental oxygen

items.q: A patient has severe hypoxaemia with a markedly increased alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient that does not improve despite a high fraction of inspired oxygen. Bilateral infiltrates are present on chest radiograph and there is no evidence of cardiac failure. Which condition best explains this?
items.a: Acute respiratory distress syndrome

items.q: Which of the following causes hypoxaemia with a NORMAL alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient?
items.a: Hypoventilation from an opioid overdose

themes.theme: Pleural fluid: Light criteria และสาเหตุ

items.q: A 16-year-old man with 1 month of low-grade fever and cough has a chest radiograph showing right upper lobe infiltration with a right pleural effusion. Pleural fluid is yellow with WBC 900 cells/dL (neutrophils 10 percent, lymphocytes 90 percent), pleural fluid to serum LDH ratio 0.8 and pleural fluid to serum protein ratio 0.7. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Tuberculous pleural effusion

items.q: A patient with fever and pleuritic chest pain has a pleural effusion. Analysis shows an exudate by Light's criteria with pleural fluid pH 7.10, glucose 35 mg/dL and LDH 1000 U/L. Gram stain shows no organisms. What is the diagnosis and the most appropriate management?
items.a: Complicated parapneumonic effusion; insert an intercostal chest drain in addition to antibiotics

items.q: Thoracentesis yields milky-white pleural fluid. Analysis shows WBC 1200 cells/microlitre with lymphocyte predominance and triglyceride 300 mg/dL. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Chylothorax

items.q: A 65-year-old smoker has 2 months of progressive breathlessness. Chest radiograph shows a mass at the right upper lobe with a massive pleural effusion. Thoracentesis shows an exudate with WBC 10,000 cells/microlitre, 90 percent mononuclear cells, and markedly elevated LDH. What is the most likely cause of the effusion?
items.a: Malignant pleural effusion from lung cancer

items.q: A patient has a bilateral pleural effusion. Pleural fluid analysis shows a transudate by Light's criteria. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
items.a: Congestive heart failure

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised cause of an amylase-rich pleural effusion?
items.a: Rheumatoid pleural effusion

themes.theme: ตรวจร่างกาย pleural effusion

items.q: A 60-year-old man has decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion at the right lower chest with decreased tactile fremitus and reduced chest wall expansion on that side. Which condition do these findings indicate?
items.a: Pleural effusion

themes.theme: Pneumothorax (tension / iatrogenic)

items.q: A 25-year-old tall thin man develops sudden right-sided chest pain and dyspnoea. Examination shows decreased breath sounds and hyperresonance to percussion on the right, with the trachea deviated to the left and blood pressure 80/50 mmHg. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
items.a: Immediate needle decompression followed by intercostal chest drain insertion

items.q: A 52-year-old woman is mechanically ventilated with pressure-controlled ventilation and PEEP for severe pneumonia. After subclavian catheterisation she develops subcutaneous emphysema and a chest radiograph shows a 10 percent right pneumothorax. What is the most appropriate management?
items.a: Tube thoracostomy

themes.theme: Re-expansion pulmonary edema

items.q: A large pleural effusion is drained and 2 litres of fluid are removed in a single session. Shortly afterwards the patient develops cough, chest tightness and worsening hypoxaemia, with new unilateral infiltrates on the side that was drained. What is the most likely complication?
items.a: Re-expansion pulmonary oedema

themes.theme: Occupational lung disease (silica, asbestos, mesothelioma, occupational asthma)

items.q: A 55-year-old man who has worked in a stone-grinding and sandblasting factory for 25 years has progressive exertional dyspnoea. Chest radiograph shows multiple small upper-zone nodules with bilateral hilar lymph nodes that have peripheral rim calcification. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Silicosis

items.q: A 60-year-old man worked for 30 years in a roofing-sheet factory. He has progressive dyspnoea and a dry cough. Chest radiograph shows irregular opacities with a fine reticular pattern in the lower zones, together with calcified pleural plaques on the diaphragmatic pleura. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Asbestosis

items.q: A 68-year-old man with a remote history of asbestos exposure presents with chest pain and a pleural effusion. Thoracentesis shows an exudate; cytology reports atypical mesothelial cells and is negative for malignant epithelial cells. What is the most likely diagnosis, and what is the principal risk factor?
items.a: Malignant pleural mesothelioma; asbestos exposure

items.q: A 35-year-old bakery worker has had wheezing and cough for 6 months. Symptoms begin a few hours after arriving at work, worsen through the working week and improve completely during weekends and holidays. Lung examination at the clinic is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis and the most important management?
items.a: Occupational asthma; remove the patient from exposure to the causative agent

themes.theme: CXR lobar pneumonia

items.q: A chest radiograph of a febrile coughing patient shows homogeneous opacification of the right lower zone containing air bronchograms, with the right heart border remaining clearly visible and no blunting of the costophrenic angle. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Lobar pneumonia of the right lower lobe

themes.theme: Lung cancer: SVC syndrome, มะเร็งที่สัมพันธ์บุหรี่

items.q: A 62-year-old man who has smoked 40 pack-years presents with facial and upper limb swelling, distended neck and chest wall veins that do not pulsate, and a right upper lobe mass on chest radiograph. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Superior vena cava syndrome from bronchogenic carcinoma

items.q: Which of the following malignancies is LEAST associated with cigarette smoking?
items.a: Breast cancer

themes.theme: Small cell lung cancer → SIADH

items.q: A 58-year-old heavy smoker is found to have a small cell lung carcinoma with mediastinal involvement. Which paraneoplastic syndrome is most characteristically associated with this tumour?
items.a: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion

items.q: A patient with small cell lung cancer has Na 118 mEq/L, urine osmolality 600 mOsm/kg, urine sodium 60 mEq/L and clinical euvolaemia with normal thyroid and adrenal function. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion

themes.theme: Pneumonia: เดาเชื้อจากเบาะแส

items.q: A 62-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes and chronic alcohol use has fever and cough productive of thick, blood-tinged sputum described as red currant jelly. Chest radiograph shows right upper lobe consolidation with a bulging fissure. Which organism is most likely responsible?
items.a: Klebsiella pneumoniae

items.q: A patient with community-acquired pneumonia has a sputum Gram stain showing gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci in pairs, with abundant polymorphonuclear leucocytes and few epithelial cells. Which antibiotic is most appropriate?
items.a: Ceftriaxone

items.q: An elderly bed-ridden man who has had a stroke with dysphagia develops fever and cough. Chest radiograph shows consolidation of the posterior segment of the right upper lobe and the superior segment of the right lower lobe. Sputum Gram stain shows mixed pleomorphic rods. Which organisms are most likely responsible?
items.a: Anaerobic oral flora

items.q: A patient who has been in the intensive care unit for 10 days is extubated after treatment for pneumonia. He develops a new fever with purulent secretions, and culture grows a gram-negative bacillus that is oxidase positive and produces a green pigment. Which organism is most likely, and which empirical therapy is appropriate?
items.a: Pseudomonas aeruginosa; an anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam such as piperacillin-tazobactam or cefepime

items.q: A previously healthy 40-year-old woman has a chronic productive cough with large volumes of purulent sputum and recurrent infections. High-resolution CT shows dilated, thick-walled bronchi. Which organism is the most common cause of infective exacerbations in a patient like this with no underlying immunodeficiency?
items.a: Haemophilus influenzae

themes.theme: CAP severity → รักษา OPD

items.q: A 40-year-old man with no comorbidity has community-acquired pneumonia. He is alert, RR 18/min, BP 122/78 mmHg, BUN 15 mg/dL and creatinine 0.87 mg/dL. What is the most appropriate management?
items.a: Outpatient treatment with high-dose oral amoxicillin

themes.theme: COPD: วินิจฉัยและรักษาระยะคงที่

items.q: A 65-year-old man with 4 months of breathlessness and greyish morning sputum has an increased anteroposterior chest diameter and normal breath sounds. Post-bronchodilator spirometry shows FEV1/FVC 68 percent with FEV1 75 percent predicted. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

items.q: A 68-year-old man with COPD remains breathless on exertion despite regular inhaled tiotropium and as-needed salbutamol, and has had two exacerbations in the past year. What is the most appropriate next step in his maintenance therapy?
items.a: Add a long-acting beta-2 agonist to make a LABA plus LAMA combination

items.q: A 65-year-old man with COPD can perform activities of daily living but becomes breathless walking more than one block. He is on appropriate inhaled therapy for his stage. SpO2 on room air is 96 percent. Which of the following is indicated in the management of this condition?
items.a: Pulmonary rehabilitation

items.q: What is the single most common precipitating cause of an acute exacerbation of COPD?
items.a: Respiratory tract infection

themes.theme: Asthma: วินิจฉัยและรักษา

items.q: A 30-year-old woman with asthma comes to the emergency department with progressive dyspnoea and non-productive cough over 3 days. She stopped her inhaled corticosteroid 3 months ago and has used her reliever inhaler every day in the past week, three times in the last hour. Vital signs: BT 37 C, PR 120/min, RR 30/min, BP 140/90 mmHg, SpO2 90 percent on room air, with generalised expiratory wheeze. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
items.a: Oxygen supplementation, systemic corticosteroid and inhaled short-acting beta-2 agonist

items.q: A 24-year-old man has had nocturnal wheeze and breathlessness almost every night for 1 week, with no daytime symptoms and no leg oedema. He has nasal congestion and rhinorrhoea every evening. Examination shows pale swollen inferior turbinates, no jugular venous distension, normal heart sounds and clear lungs. What is the most likely cause of his breathlessness?
items.a: Asthma

items.q: A 28-year-old woman with asthma has symptoms twice a week and wakes at night once or twice a month. She currently uses only an as-needed short-acting beta-2 agonist. According to current asthma guidelines, what should she be prescribed?
items.a: As-needed low-dose inhaled corticosteroid-formoterol as reliever therapy

items.q: Which test best confirms the diagnosis of asthma in a patient with intermittent wheeze and a normal physical examination in the clinic?
items.a: Spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility testing

themes.theme: Hypercalcemia: PHPT, มะเร็ง, myeloma, ลำดับการรักษา

items.q: What is the most common cause of hypercalcaemia in the outpatient setting?
items.a: Primary hyperparathyroidism

items.q: A 70-year-old asymptomatic man has calcium 11.0 mg/dL (8.6-10.2) and phosphate 1.1 mg/dL (2.7-4.5) with no drug history. What is the most likely cause?
items.a: Primary hyperparathyroidism

items.q: A patient with bone metastases presents with drowsiness, polyuria and constipation. Which electrolyte abnormality is most likely?
items.a: Hypercalcaemia

items.q: A woman has calcium 12.5 mg/dL with phosphate 1.9 mg/dL and elevated intact PTH. What is the mechanism?
items.a: Excess parathyroid hormone increasing bone resorption, renal calcium reabsorption and phosphate excretion

items.q: A patient with metastatic cancer has calcium 14 mg/dL, drowsiness and creatinine 2.4 mg/dL. What is the correct order of treatment?
items.a: Intravenous isotonic saline first, then a bisphosphonate (with calcitonin for rapid effect)

items.q: A 77-year-old woman has severe back pain, anaemia, creatinine 2.8 mg/dL and calcium 12.8 mg/dL with lytic bone lesions. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Multiple myeloma

themes.theme: Tumor lysis syndrome

items.q: Which finding is NOT expected in tumour lysis syndrome?
items.a: Hypercalcaemia

items.q: A patient with acute leukaemia develops K 5.6 mEq/L, calcium 7.8 mg/dL, phosphate 6.8 mg/dL and creatinine rising 1 day after the first chemotherapy. What is the diagnosis and the key preventive measure?
items.a: Tumour lysis syndrome; aggressive intravenous hydration with rasburicase or allopurinol in high-risk patients

items.q: A patient develops acute kidney injury with hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia and hyperuricaemia 2 days after starting chemotherapy. What is the mechanism of the renal injury?
items.a: Uric acid and calcium phosphate crystal deposition in the tubules from tumour lysis

themes.theme: Hypocalcemia: สาเหตุ

items.q: What is the most common cause of hypocalcaemia in adults?
items.a: Iatrogenic post-surgical hypoparathyroidism (e.g. after thyroidectomy)

items.q: What is the main mechanism of hypocalcaemia in end-stage renal disease?
items.a: Phosphate retention with reduced calcitriol production by the failing kidney

items.q: Which electrolyte falls as a result of citrate toxicity after massive blood transfusion?
items.a: Ionised calcium

items.q: A patient with a round face, short stature and shortened fourth metacarpals has low calcium, high phosphate and a high PTH level. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Pseudohypoparathyroidism (Albright hereditary osteodystrophy)

themes.theme: Magnesium และ hypoK ดื้อ (amphotericin)

items.q: A 16-year-old girl with leukaemia on prolonged amphotericin B has persistent hypokalaemia despite daily potassium replacement. Which additional test is most useful?
items.a: Serum magnesium

items.q: A patient with HIV on amphotericin B for 1 week develops proximal muscle weakness grade 3. Which investigation should be sent first?
items.a: Serum electrolytes including potassium and magnesium

items.q: Which statement about magnesium is correct?
items.a: Hypomagnesaemia causes refractory hypokalaemia and hypocalcaemia and must be corrected first

themes.theme: Nephrotic syndrome: นิยาม/ตรวจปัสสาวะ

items.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the diagnostic criteria for nephrotic syndrome?
items.a: Haematuria

items.q: A patient has foamy urine, periorbital oedema and urine microscopy showing oval fat bodies and fatty casts. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Nephrotic syndrome

items.q: Which test is most appropriate to quantify proteinuria in a patient with suspected nephrotic syndrome?
items.a: Spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (or 24-hour urine protein)

items.q: A patient presents with periorbital and bilateral leg oedema with very foamy urine. Which investigation should be ordered first?
items.a: Urinalysis with urine sediment examination

items.q: Fatty casts and oval fat bodies in the urine indicate which condition?
items.a: Nephrotic syndrome

themes.theme: Nephrotic: ภาวะแทรกซ้อน VTE

items.q: Which complication is characteristic of nephrotic syndrome?
items.a: Venous thromboembolism from urinary loss of antithrombin III

themes.theme: Glomerular disease ตามบริบท (MN-มะเร็ง, MCD, HIVAN, heroin, myeloma)

items.q: A 55-year-old man with nephrotic syndrome and microscopic haematuria is found to have an underlying solid organ malignancy. Which glomerular lesion is most likely?
items.a: Membranous nephropathy

items.q: A 20-year-old man has sudden onset generalised oedema with nephrotic-range proteinuria, normal renal function and no haematuria. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Minimal change disease

items.q: A 25-year-old man with untreated HIV has 24-hour urine protein 12 g and ultrasound showing bilaterally enlarged echogenic kidneys. What is the most likely lesion?
items.a: Collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (HIV-associated nephropathy)

items.q: A 37-year-old man with generalised oedema, albumin 2.8 g/dL, urine protein 3+ without significant RBC or WBC, and linear scars over the arms has which likely underlying cause?
items.a: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis related to intravenous drug use

items.q: A 65-year-old man has 3 months of malaise, Hct 25 percent, BUN/Cr 22/1.8 mg/dL, K 3.0 mEq/L, HCO3 18 mEq/L and 24-hour urine protein 3 g with a negative dipstick for albumin. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Multiple myeloma with light chain (cast) nephropathy

themes.theme: Urine cast บอกตำแหน่ง (RBC/WBC/muddy brown)

items.q: Red blood cells in the urine with dysmorphic forms and red cell casts indicate bleeding from which site?
items.a: The glomerulus

items.q: Muddy brown granular casts in the urine are most characteristic of which condition?
items.a: Acute tubular necrosis

items.q: Which urinary finding supports intrinsic acute kidney injury from tubular injury?
items.a: Granular casts with renal tubular epithelial cells

items.q: White blood cell casts in the urine indicate inflammation at which site?
items.a: The renal parenchyma — pyelonephritis or acute interstitial nephritis

themes.theme: Hematuria: glomerular vs urologic

items.q: Which finding argues AGAINST a glomerular source of haematuria?
items.a: Blood clots in the urine

items.q: A 65-year-old smoker has painless gross haematuria with normal renal function. Which investigation confirms the diagnosis?
items.a: Cystoscopy (with CT urography)

items.q: Which approach is correct when evaluating haematuria?
items.a: Confirm true haematuria with microscopy, then classify as glomerular or non-glomerular before imaging or cystoscopy

themes.theme: ชนิด proteinuria (glomerular/functional/orthostatic)

items.q: A patient with generalised oedema has 2.5 g proteinuria per day with a bland urine sediment. Which mechanism of proteinuria is most likely?
items.a: Glomerular proteinuria from increased glomerular permeability

items.q: A healthy young man has 1+ proteinuria after exercise, which disappears on a repeat sample taken at rest. What is the diagnosis and management?
items.a: Functional (exercise-induced) proteinuria; reassure and check annually

items.q: Which statement about orthostatic proteinuria is correct?
items.a: Protein excretion is normal in the recumbent first morning sample and less than 1 g per day overall, with a benign prognosis

themes.theme: Acute nephritic: PSGN vs IgA

items.q: A 30-year-old man has headache and cola-coloured urine 2 weeks after pharyngitis, with BP 180/110 mmHg, periorbital oedema, RBC casts and low C3. What is the diagnosis and treatment?
items.a: Acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis; salt and water restriction with antihypertensive therapy and penicillin for residual infection

items.q: Urinalysis shows RBC 50-100/HPF with dysmorphic forms, trace protein, no glucose and WBC 0-1/HPF. Which set of differential diagnoses is most appropriate?
items.a: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, IgA nephropathy and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis

items.q: Which feature best distinguishes IgA nephropathy from post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis?
items.a: Haematuria occurring within 1-2 days of an upper respiratory infection with normal complement levels

themes.theme: Lupus nephritis

items.q: A young woman with a photosensitive rash and arthritis has urine protein 3+ with RBC 30-50/HPF. What is the most likely diagnosis and the next step?
items.a: Lupus nephritis; send ANA, anti-dsDNA, complement levels and arrange renal biopsy

items.q: Urine sediment shows oval fat bodies together with dysmorphic red blood cells in a young woman with arthritis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Lupus nephritis with a mixed nephrotic-nephritic picture

items.q: Urinalysis shows proteinuria, microscopic haematuria and pyuria in a young woman with a malar rash. What is the interpretation?
items.a: Glomerulonephritis, most likely lupus nephritis

items.q: Which urine finding indicates significant proteinuria with lipiduria in lupus nephritis?
items.a: Oval fat bodies with a Maltese cross appearance under polarised light

themes.theme: CKD vs AKI: ไตเล็ก = เรื้อรัง

items.q: Which ultrasound finding best distinguishes chronic kidney disease from acute kidney injury?
items.a: Small kidneys (less than 9 cm) with thin cortex and increased echogenicity bilaterally

items.q: Which investigation is most useful to establish chronicity when the duration of renal impairment is unknown?
items.a: Renal ultrasound

items.q: A patient has shrunken kidneys of 6 cm with a thin cortex bilaterally and eGFR 8 mL/min/1.73 m2. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: End-stage kidney disease requiring preparation for renal replacement therapy

items.q: Which finding indicates chronicity rather than an acute process in renal failure?
items.a: Renal osteodystrophy with hyperphosphataemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism

themes.theme: eGFR / Cockcroft-Gault

items.q: Which statement about estimated GFR is correct?
items.a: eGFR equations use serum creatinine with age and sex, and are unreliable when creatinine is changing rapidly

items.q: A 40-year-old man weighing 70 kg has creatinine 1.5 mg/dL. Which formula estimates creatinine clearance at the bedside?
items.a: Cockcroft-Gault: (140 - age) x weight / (72 x serum creatinine), multiplied by 0.85 in women

themes.theme: Metformin กับ eGFR

items.q: Which oral antidiabetic drug must be stopped when eGFR falls below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2?
items.a: Metformin

themes.theme: Crystal arthritis: gout / CPPD / BCP

items.q: Synovial fluid from a painful knee contains rhomboid-shaped crystals that are weakly positively birefringent under polarized light. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease (pseudogout)

items.q: In the same patient with pseudogout of the knee, which additional synovial fluid profile is expected?
items.a: Inflammatory fluid with WBC 2,000-50,000/mm3, predominantly neutrophils, and reduced viscosity

items.q: A 50-year-old man with acute pain of the first metatarsophalangeal joint has synovial fluid showing needle-shaped, strongly negatively birefringent crystals. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Acute gouty arthritis

items.q: Which drug is the most appropriate first-line treatment for an acute gout flare in a patient with peptic ulcer disease?
items.a: Colchicine

items.q: Which radiographic finding is most characteristic of long-standing tophaceous gout?
items.a: Punched-out erosion with sclerotic margin and overhanging edge, with preserved joint space

items.q: Which of the following is an indication to start urate-lowering therapy?
items.a: Presence of tophi or two or more gout flares per year

items.q: A 70-year-old man on hemodialysis develops an acutely painful shoulder. Aspiration shows no crystals under polarized light but the fluid contains clumps that stain with alizarin red. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Basic calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite) associated arthritis

items.q: Which drug is most appropriate for an acute gout flare in a patient with CKD stage 3 and peptic ulcer disease?
items.a: Oral prednisolone (or low-dose colchicine with dose adjustment)

themes.theme: NSAID กับไต

items.q: A patient's creatinine rises after taking diclofenac for knee pain. Which drug should be stopped first?
items.a: Diclofenac

items.q: What is the mechanism of NSAID-induced acute kidney injury?
items.a: Inhibition of prostaglandin-mediated afferent arteriolar vasodilatation reducing glomerular filtration

themes.theme: Uremia และข้อบ่งชี้ dialysis

items.q: Which clinical feature is a manifestation of uraemia in advanced chronic kidney disease?
items.a: Pericardial friction rub with nausea, pruritus and asterixis

items.q: What are the indications for urgent dialysis?
items.a: Refractory acidosis, electrolyte disturbance (severe hyperkalaemia), intoxication, fluid overload and uraemic complications

items.q: Which is an indication for dialysis in rhabdomyolysis-associated acute kidney injury?
items.a: Refractory hyperkalaemia, severe acidosis or fluid overload not responding to medical therapy

themes.theme: Hyponatremia: approach และแก้อย่างปลอดภัย (ODS, thiazide, pseudo)

items.q: A hypertensive patient on hydrochlorothiazide presents with drowsiness and weakness with Na 105 mEq/L. What is the most appropriate management?
items.a: Stop the thiazide and correct sodium slowly, using hypertonic saline only if there are severe neurological symptoms

items.q: Before choosing therapy for hyponatraemia, which assessment is most important?
items.a: Volume status together with serum and urine osmolality and urine sodium

items.q: A patient has Na 114 mEq/L and K 4.1 mEq/L. Which treatment is NOT indicated?
items.a: Potassium supplementation

items.q: A patient with chronic hyponatraemia corrected rapidly with 3% saline develops dysarthria, quadriparesis and impaired consciousness several days later. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Osmotic demyelination syndrome

items.q: A patient has Na 130 mEq/L with plasma glucose 600 mg/dL. How should the sodium be interpreted?
items.a: Translocational hyponatraemia — corrected sodium is about 138 mEq/L

themes.theme: Adrenal insufficiency

items.q: A woman with severe postpartum haemorrhage later develops fatigue, failure to lactate and hyponatraemia. What is the mechanism?
items.a: Secondary adrenal insufficiency from pituitary infarction (Sheehan syndrome) with loss of ACTH

items.q: A patient with hyperpigmentation, postural hypotension, Na 128 mEq/L and K 5.9 mEq/L has which diagnosis?
items.a: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease)

themes.theme: Periodic paralysis / K shift (thyrotoxic)

items.q: What is the main mechanism of hypokalaemia in thyrotoxic periodic paralysis?
items.a: Transcellular shift of potassium into cells driven by increased Na-K-ATPase activity

items.q: A young Asian man wakes with proximal muscle weakness. K 1.9 mEq/L, TSH suppressed with high free T4. What is the management?
items.a: Careful potassium replacement with propranolol and definitive treatment of thyrotoxicosis

items.q: A young man develops transient weakness with K 2.6 mEq/L after a large carbohydrate meal and alcohol at a party, with normal acid-base status and rapid recovery after potassium replacement. What is the mechanism?
items.a: Transcellular potassium shift driven by insulin and catecholamines

items.q: A patient develops episodic weakness after a large meal with K 6.2 mEq/L and normal renal function. What is the likely diagnosis?
items.a: Hyperkalaemic periodic paralysis

items.q: A patient has proximal muscle weakness with K 2.4 mEq/L and a suppressed TSH. What is the complete diagnosis?
items.a: Hypokalaemic muscle weakness from thyrotoxicosis (thyrotoxic periodic paralysis)

themes.theme: Electrolyte กับอาการชัก

items.q: Which electrolyte abnormality is LEAST likely to cause seizures or altered consciousness?
items.a: Hypokalaemia

themes.theme: HypoK อื่น ๆ (leptospirosis, ECG U wave)

items.q: By which mechanism does leptospirosis cause hypokalaemia?
items.a: Renal potassium wasting from tubular dysfunction (impaired sodium reabsorption in the proximal tubule)

items.q: Which ECG change is characteristic of hypokalaemia?
items.a: Flattened T waves with prominent U waves and ST depression

themes.theme: Fanconi syndrome

items.q: A patient has glucosuria with normal blood glucose, phosphaturia, aminoaciduria and normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Fanconi syndrome (generalised proximal tubular dysfunction)

themes.theme: นิ่วไต (calcium oxalate, struvite/Proteus, uric)

items.q: A 29-year-old man with right flank pain radiating to the groin has urine RBC 100-200/HPF, uric acid 8.5 mg/dL and a normal plain KUB film. Which management is INAPPROPRIATE?
items.a: Giving probenecid to lower the serum uric acid

items.q: Which type of kidney stone is the most common overall?
items.a: Calcium oxalate

items.q: A KUB radiograph shows bilateral staghorn calculi filling the renal pelvis. Which urinary finding is most specific?
items.a: Coffin-lid shaped triple phosphate (struvite) crystals with alkaline urine

items.q: A patient with recurrent urinary tract infections has nitrite-positive urine and a staghorn stone in the left renal pelvis. Which organism is most likely?
items.a: Proteus mirabilis (a urease-producing organism)

items.q: A patient with recurrent cystitis has nitrite-positive urine and a staghorn stone. What is the definitive management?
items.a: Complete surgical removal of the stone with antibiotic therapy

themes.theme: Asymptomatic bacteriuria: รักษาเมื่อไร

items.q: A pregnant woman at 12 weeks has asymptomatic bacteriuria with more than 100,000 CFU/mL of E. coli. What is the management?
items.a: Treat with a pregnancy-safe antibiotic such as amoxicillin, cephalexin or nitrofurantoin (avoid in the third trimester) and repeat the culture

items.q: A woman with diabetes has a routine urinalysis showing WBC more than 100/HPF with many bacteria but no symptoms. What is the appropriate management?
items.a: Observation without antibiotics

items.q: An elderly woman with an indwelling catheter and bacteriuria develops agitation and confusion. What is the most appropriate approach?
items.a: Search systematically for other causes of delirium before attributing it to the bacteriuria

themes.theme: Simple cystitis (เกณฑ์ culture, ยาสั้น)

items.q: What quantitative threshold on urine culture supports the diagnosis of urinary tract infection in a symptomatic woman with a clean-catch specimen?
items.a: At least 10^5 CFU/mL of a single uropathogen (10^2-10^3 may suffice with typical symptoms)

items.q: A healthy young woman has 2 days of dysuria and frequency without fever or flank pain. What is the best management?
items.a: A short course of oral antibiotics for uncomplicated cystitis, guided by local resistance patterns

themes.theme: UTI: เดาเชื้อจาก gram stain / สายสวน

items.q: A man with three urinary tract infections in 1 year has nitrite 1+ and a Gram stain showing gram-negative bacilli. Which organism is most likely?
items.a: Escherichia coli

items.q: Which organism is suggested by nitrite-positive urine with gram-negative bacilli on Gram stain?
items.a: A member of the Enterobacteriaceae such as E. coli or Klebsiella

items.q: A patient with a long-term indwelling urinary catheter has a urinary tract infection with gram-positive cocci in chains. Which organism is most likely?
items.a: Enterococcus faecalis

themes.theme: เบาหวานกับ UTI (รวม SGLT2i)

items.q: Which factor increases the risk of complicated urinary tract infection in a diabetic patient?
items.a: Glycosuria with impaired neutrophil function and possible neurogenic bladder

items.q: Which antidiabetic drug increases the risk of genitourinary infection?
items.a: SGLT2 inhibitor

themes.theme: UTI ซ้ำในผู้ชาย → ตรวจต่อมลูกหมาก

items.q: An elderly man with recurrent urinary tract infections and perineal discomfort should have which examination?
items.a: Digital rectal examination to assess the prostate, with post-void residual measurement

themes.theme: Pyelonephritis ซับซ้อน (abscess, de-escalate, sepsis AKI)

items.q: A patient with acute pyelonephritis remains febrile after 72 hours of appropriate intravenous antibiotics. Ultrasound shows a renal abscess. What is the management?
items.a: Continue antibiotics and arrange drainage (percutaneous or surgical) for source control

items.q: After starting empirical meropenem for pyelonephritis, culture grows E. coli sensitive to ceftriaxone. What should be done?
items.a: De-escalate to ceftriaxone according to the culture result

items.q: A patient in the ICU has confusion, T 38.5 C, BP 80/50 mmHg, PR 140/min, Na 122, K 3.9, HCO3 21, BUN 45 and Cr 1.7 mg/dL with pyuria. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Sepsis from acute pyelonephritis with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury

themes.theme: Cyclophosphamide hemorrhagic cystitis

items.q: Which chemotherapeutic agent causes haemorrhagic cystitis, and what prevents it?
items.a: Cyclophosphamide or ifosfamide; prevented by hydration and mesna

themes.theme: Purple urine bag syndrome

items.q: A bedridden patient with a long-term catheter has purple discolouration of the urine bag. What is the cause?
items.a: Purple urine bag syndrome from bacterial indoxyl sulfate metabolism in alkaline urine

themes.theme: Renal TB (sterile pyuria)

items.q: A patient with sterile pyuria and chronic urinary symptoms from a TB-endemic area should have which investigation?
items.a: Urine for acid-fast bacilli and molecular testing (Xpert MTB/RIF) on early morning samples

themes.theme: Prerenal vs ATN (FENa, cast, กลไก)

items.q: A dehydrated patient has BUN/creatinine ratio above 20, urine sodium 12 mEq/L, FENa 0.5 percent and hyaline casts. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Prerenal azotaemia

items.q: What is the main mechanism of drug-induced acute tubular necrosis?
items.a: Ischaemic and direct toxic injury to tubular epithelial cells

items.q: A woman with 1 month of heavy menstrual bleeding has Hct 21 percent, BP 90/60 mmHg and creatinine rising to 2.2 mg/dL with FENa 0.4 percent. What is the mechanism of her acute kidney injury?
items.a: Renal hypoperfusion (prerenal) from blood loss

items.q: A woman with myoma uteri has heavy vaginal bleeding, hypotension and oliguria with rising creatinine. What is the most appropriate initial management?
items.a: Restore intravascular volume with fluid and blood transfusion while controlling the bleeding

items.q: Which cause of reduced GFR is functional (haemodynamic) rather than structural?
items.a: Prerenal azotaemia from hypovolaemia, heart failure or cirrhosis

items.q: Which urinary index favours acute tubular necrosis over prerenal azotaemia?
items.a: FENa above 2 percent with urine osmolality below 350 mOsm/kg

themes.theme: Rhabdomyolysis / statin myopathy (CK)

items.q: A patient on simvastatin and gemfibrozil develops severe muscle pain, dark urine, CK 45,000 U/L and creatinine 3.5 mg/dL. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Rhabdomyolysis with myoglobinuric acute kidney injury

items.q: Which investigation confirms rhabdomyolysis?
items.a: Serum creatine kinase

items.q: A patient with statin-fibrate rhabdomyolysis has K 6.8 mEq/L, phosphate 8 mg/dL, creatinine 4.2 mg/dL and CK 60,000 U/L. What is the management priority?
items.a: Stop the offending drugs, give aggressive intravenous isotonic fluid and treat hyperkalaemia, with dialysis if refractory

items.q: A 58-year-old man on simvastatin complains of symmetric proximal muscle aching. Which investigation should be ordered first?
items.a: Serum creatine kinase

items.q: A patient has proximal muscle weakness with AST 1,000 U/L but normal ALT, ALP and GGT. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
items.a: Creatine kinase

themes.theme: Contrast-associated AKI

items.q: A patient with CKD needs a contrast CT. What is the best evidence-based prophylaxis against contrast-associated acute kidney injury?
items.a: Intravenous isotonic saline before and after the scan with the lowest possible contrast dose and withholding nephrotoxic drugs

themes.theme: Obstructive AKI (BPH)

items.q: An elderly man with benign prostatic hyperplasia has anuria, a palpable bladder and rising creatinine. What is the first management step?
items.a: Bladder catheterisation to relieve the obstruction

themes.theme: Lithium nephrogenic DI

items.q: A 64-year-old man on lithium for 20 years has polyuria with low urine osmolality that does not rise after desmopressin. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

themes.theme: SJS จาก allopurinol (HLA-B*58:01)

items.q: A patient develops Stevens-Johnson syndrome after receiving allopurinol. Testing for which allele would have identified the risk before prescribing?
A patient taking allopurinol develops a widespread painful rash with erosions of the lips, oral mucosa and conjunctivae, with skin detachment of about 8% of body surface area. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Stevens-Johnson syndrome

themes.theme: Transfusion reaction

items.q: Fifteen minutes after a packed red cell transfusion is started, a patient develops itchy urticarial wheals only, with no fever, no hypotension and normal urine colour. What is the most likely type of reaction?
items.a: Allergic (urticarial) transfusion reaction

items.q: A patient develops fever and chills 2 hours into a red cell transfusion. Urine colour is normal, blood pressure is stable and there is no flank pain. What is the most likely diagnosis and the measure to prevent recurrence?
items.a: Febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reaction; use leukocyte-reduced blood components in future transfusions

themes.theme: Immune cytopenia → หา SLE/HIV/HCV

items.q: A 25-year-old woman has anemia and jaundice. Blood smear shows spherocytes and polychromasia; direct Coombs test is positive. Which additional investigation should be sent to look for an underlying cause?
items.a: Antinuclear antibody

items.q: A newly diagnosed HIV-positive man has isolated thrombocytopenia (platelet 80,000/mm3) with normal hemoglobin and white cell count, and no bleeding. What is the most appropriate management?
items.a: Start antiretroviral therapy and monitor the platelet count

items.q: A young woman presents with easy bruising for 1 week. CBC shows isolated thrombocytopenia with giant platelets on smear; hemoglobin and white cells are normal. Besides a bone marrow study if indicated, which screening tests are most appropriate to look for secondary causes?
items.a: Antinuclear antibody, anti-HIV and anti-hepatitis C virus

themes.theme: ผลข้างเคียงยากดภูมิใน SLE (วัคซีน, DM, HCQ ตา, AVN, MMF ตั้งครรภ์)

items.q: A patient on long-term prednisolone 30 mg daily for lupus nephritis asks about vaccination. Which vaccine is contraindicated?
items.a: Live attenuated varicella vaccine

items.q: A woman with SLE has been on prednisolone for 3 years and now presents in pregnancy with fasting plasma glucose 138 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.2% at 8 weeks of gestation. How should her hyperglycemia be classified?
items.a: Pre-existing (overt) diabetes mellitus detected in pregnancy, likely glucocorticoid-induced

items.q: Which drug used in systemic lupus erythematosus requires periodic ophthalmologic screening because of the risk of irreversible maculopathy?
items.a: Hydroxychloroquine

items.q: A 34-year-old woman with SLE on long-term high-dose prednisolone develops progressive right groin pain on weight bearing. Hip radiograph is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
items.a: MRI of both hips

items.q: A woman with SLE and lupus nephritis wishes to become pregnant. Which drug must be stopped and replaced before conception?
items.a: Mycophenolate mofetil, replaced by azathioprine

themes.theme: จำแนก arthritis (OA/RA/SpA/AOSD/chikungunya)
