items.q: A 20-year-old man presents with fever, arthralgia, a maculopapular rash over the trunk and extremities, and swelling with warmth and limited movement of both knees, ankles and elbows. Hct 40%, WBC 3,500/mm3 (N 45%, L 50%, atypical lymphocyte 5%), platelet 45,000/mm3. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Chikungunya virus infection

items.q: A 60-year-old woman has bilateral knee pain worse with walking, relieved by rest, with 10 minutes of morning stiffness and bony enlargement of the distal interphalangeal joints. ANA and rheumatoid factor are negative. Radiograph shows joint space narrowing with osteophytes. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Osteoarthritis

items.q: A 46-year-old woman has symmetric swelling of the MCP and PIP joints of both hands with morning stiffness of more than 30 minutes for 4 months. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Rheumatoid arthritis

items.q: A 27-year-old man has chronic low back pain that improves with exercise, wakes him in the early morning, with morning stiffness of 1 hour and a past episode of acute anterior uveitis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Axial spondyloarthritis (ankylosing spondylitis)

items.q: A 28-year-old woman has daily evening fever for 3 weeks, an evanescent salmon-coloured rash, sore throat, arthralgia, neutrophilic leukocytosis and ferritin 8,000 ng/mL, with negative ANA, RF and blood cultures. What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.a: Adult-onset Still disease

themes.theme: เลือก autoantibody (ANA, dsDNA/Sm, drug-induced, APS, Scl-70, ANCA)

items.q: Which of the following is the best initial screening test in a patient with suspected systemic lupus erythematosus?
items.a: Antinuclear antibody

items.q: A 45-year-old woman on hydralazine for 1 year develops arthralgia, fever and pleuritic chest pain. ANA is positive, anti-double-stranded DNA is negative, anti-histone antibody is positive and complement levels are normal. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Drug-induced lupus erythematosus

items.q: A woman with four unexplained pregnancy losses and a past unprovoked deep vein thrombosis is suspected of having antiphospholipid syndrome. Which antibody should be tested?
items.a: Anticardiolipin antibody (with lupus anticoagulant and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I)

items.q: A patient with features of systemic sclerosis has a negative ANA on the standard screening assay. Which test should be sent next?
items.a: Anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70) and anticentromere antibodies

items.q: A 56-year-old man with chronic sinusitis and bloody nasal discharge develops hemoptysis, cavitating lung nodules and glomerulonephritis with red cell casts. Which antibody is most likely to be positive?
items.a: Anti-proteinase 3 (c-ANCA)

items.q: Which antibody pattern is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
items.a: Anti-Smith and anti-double-stranded DNA

themes.theme: Septic / gonococcal arthritis

items.q: A patient with a hot swollen knee has synovial fluid Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci in clusters. What is the most appropriate antibiotic?
items.a: Intravenous cloxacillin

items.q: A patient with septic arthritis on intravenous cloxacillin for 12 days is clinically well but the neutrophil count has fallen to 900/mm3. What is the most appropriate next step?
items.a: Recognize drug-induced neutropenia and switch to another effective antibiotic class with monitoring

items.q: A 45-year-old man presents with acute arthritis. Which of the following history items is most important to obtain?
items.a: Sexual history, alcohol intake, recent infection and family history of arthritis

items.q: A 30-year-old sexually active man has migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis of the wrist and a few pustular skin lesions, then develops a hot swollen knee. What is the most likely organism?
items.a: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

themes.theme: Scleroderma renal crisis

items.q: A patient with diffuse systemic sclerosis recently started on prednisolone develops blood pressure 210/120 mmHg, acute kidney injury and schistocytes on blood smear. Which drug should be started immediately?
items.a: Captopril

themes.theme: Dermatomyositis → หามะเร็ง

items.q: A 55-year-old woman has proximal muscle weakness, a violaceous periorbital rash and scaly papules over the knuckles. Apart from treating the myositis, what must not be missed?
items.a: Screening for an underlying malignancy

themes.theme: GCA / PMR

items.q: A 72-year-old woman has new temporal headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication and ESR 95 mm/hr. Vision is normal. What should be done first?
items.a: Start high-dose corticosteroid immediately, then arrange temporal artery biopsy

items.q: A 68-year-old woman has 2 months of bilateral shoulder and hip girdle aching with prolonged morning stiffness, ESR 88 mm/hr, normal creatine kinase and no true weakness on testing. What is the most likely diagnosis and treatment?
items.a: Polymyalgia rheumatica; low-dose prednisolone 12.5-25 mg daily with a dramatic response expected

themes.theme: IgA vasculitis (HSP)

items.q: A 19-year-old man has palpable purpura over both legs and buttocks, colicky abdominal pain, arthralgia and hematuria one week after an upper respiratory infection. Platelet count and coagulation tests are normal. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schonlein purpura)

themes.theme: ความปลอดภัย DMARD/biologic ใน RA

items.q: Which conventional DMARD is the anchor drug for newly diagnosed rheumatoid arthritis, and how is it given?
items.a: Methotrexate, given once weekly with folic acid supplementation

items.q: Before starting an anti-TNF biologic agent in rheumatoid arthritis, which screening is mandatory?
items.a: Latent tuberculosis (chest radiograph plus tuberculin skin test or IGRA) and hepatitis B and C serology

items.q: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate develops fever, dry cough and diffuse interstitial infiltrates with leukopenia. What should be done first?
items.a: Stop methotrexate and evaluate for both opportunistic infection and drug-induced pneumonitis

new_themes.theme: Myocarditis: สาเหตุส่วนใหญ่คือไวรัส

items.q: What is the most common cause of myocarditis in previously healthy adults?
items.a: Viral infection

items.a: Aortic stenosis

items.a: A single dose of clindamycin or azithromycin before the procedure

items.a: ACE inhibitor such as enalapril

items.a: Class II

items.q: A patient completing anti-tuberculous therapy notices that his urine, tears and sweat have turned orange-red. He feels well and liver function tests are normal. Which drug is responsible?

items.a: High anion gap metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation

items.q: A patient has a bilateral pleural effusion. Pleural fluid analysis shows a transudate by Light's criteria. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
items.a: Congestive heart failure

items.a: Anaerobic oral flora

items.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the diagnostic criteria for nephrotic syndrome?
items.a: Haematuria

new_themes.theme: CKD vs AKI: ไตเล็ก = เรื้อรัง

items.a: Renal osteodystrophy with hyperphosphataemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism

items.a: Hyperkalaemic periodic paralysis

items.a: A short course of oral antibiotics for uncomplicated cystitis, guided by local resistance patterns

items.q: Which ECG pattern is most characteristic of acute pericarditis rather than myocardial infarction?
items.a: Widespread concave ST elevation with PR depression and no reciprocal change

items.q: An ECG shows ST elevation in II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL, rate 75/min, sinus rhythm and narrow QRS. What is the complete interpretation?
items.a: Normal sinus rhythm with acute inferior wall ST-elevation myocardial infarction

items.a: A 60-year-old man 2 weeks after an acute ischaemic stroke of atherosclerotic origin

items.q: A 28-year-old asymptomatic man has a strong family history of premature coronary disease. Which investigation is most appropriate first?
items.a: Fasting lipid profile

new_themes.theme: Small cell lung cancer → SIADH

items.q: A 58-year-old heavy smoker is found to have a small cell lung carcinoma with mediastinal involvement. Which paraneoplastic syndrome is most characteristically associated with this tumour?
items.a: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion

new_themes.theme: SJS จาก allopurinol (HLA-B*58:01)

items.q: A patient develops Stevens-Johnson syndrome after receiving allopurinol. Testing for which allele would have identified the risk before prescribing?
A patient taking allopurinol develops a widespread painful rash with erosions of the lips, oral mucosa and conjunctivae, with skin detachment of about 8% of body surface area. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Stevens-Johnson syndrome

new_themes.theme: Transfusion reaction

items.q: Fifteen minutes after a packed red cell transfusion is started, a patient develops itchy urticarial wheals only, with no fever, no hypotension and normal urine colour. What is the most likely type of reaction?
items.a: Allergic (urticarial) transfusion reaction

items.q: A patient develops fever and chills 2 hours into a red cell transfusion. Urine colour is normal, blood pressure is stable and there is no flank pain. What is the most likely diagnosis and the measure to prevent recurrence?
items.a: Febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reaction; use leukocyte-reduced blood components in future transfusions

new_themes.theme: Immune cytopenia → หา SLE/HIV/HCV

items.q: A 25-year-old woman has anemia and jaundice. Blood smear shows spherocytes and polychromasia; direct Coombs test is positive. Which additional investigation should be sent to look for an underlying cause?
items.a: Antinuclear antibody

new_themes.theme: เลือก autoantibody (ANA, dsDNA/Sm, drug-induced, APS, Scl-70, ANCA)

items.q: A 45-year-old woman on hydralazine for 1 year develops arthralgia, fever and pleuritic chest pain. ANA is positive, anti-double-stranded DNA is negative, anti-histone antibody is positive and complement levels are normal. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Drug-induced lupus erythematosus

items.q: A woman with four unexplained pregnancy losses and a past unprovoked deep vein thrombosis is suspected of having antiphospholipid syndrome. Which antibody should be tested?
items.a: Anticardiolipin antibody (with lupus anticoagulant and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I)

items.q: A patient with features of systemic sclerosis has a negative ANA on the standard screening assay. Which test should be sent next?
items.a: Anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70) and anticentromere antibodies

new_themes.theme: Septic / gonococcal arthritis

items.q: A patient with a hot swollen knee has synovial fluid Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci in clusters. What is the most appropriate antibiotic?
items.a: Intravenous cloxacillin

items.q: A patient with septic arthritis on intravenous cloxacillin for 12 days is clinically well but the neutrophil count has fallen to 900/mm3. What is the most appropriate next step?
items.a: Recognize drug-induced neutropenia and switch to another effective antibiotic class with monitoring

items.q: A 45-year-old man presents with acute arthritis. Which of the following history items is most important to obtain?
items.a: Sexual history, alcohol intake, recent infection and family history of arthritis

items.q: A 30-year-old sexually active man has migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis of the wrist and a few pustular skin lesions, then develops a hot swollen knee. What is the most likely organism?
items.a: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

new_themes.theme: Dermatomyositis → หามะเร็ง

items.q: A 55-year-old woman has proximal muscle weakness, a violaceous periorbital rash and scaly papules over the knuckles. Apart from treating the myositis, what must not be missed?
items.a: Screening for an underlying malignancy

new_themes.theme: ความปลอดภัย DMARD/biologic ใน RA

items.q: Which conventional DMARD is the anchor drug for newly diagnosed rheumatoid arthritis, and how is it given?
items.a: Methotrexate, given once weekly with folic acid supplementation

new_themes.theme: Cardiorenal / high-output state

items.q: A patient with heart failure has worsening congestion and a rising creatinine. What is the most appropriate management of type 1 cardiorenal syndrome?
items.a: Continue decongestion with intravenous loop diuretic and salt restriction, monitoring renal function

items.q: A patient has warm hands and feet, wide pulse pressure, rising creatinine and a preserved ejection fraction with high cardiac output. Which mechanism best explains the picture?
items.a: A high-output state with systemic vasodilatation and inadequate effective organ perfusion

items.q: A patient with heart failure and CKD has worsening congestion with rising creatinine. What is the appropriate approach?
items.a: Salt restriction with intravenous loop diuretic to achieve decongestion, and dialysis if diuretic-resistant

items.q: A patient with warm extremities, wide pulse pressure, rising creatinine and preserved ejection fraction most likely has which problem?
items.a: Inadequate effective organ perfusion in a high-output vasodilated state (e.g. sepsis, cirrhosis)

items.q: In cardiorenal syndrome type 1, which factor most drives the fall in renal function?
items.a: Venous congestion with raised central venous pressure

new_themes.theme: CAP severity → รักษา OPD

items.q: A 40-year-old man with no comorbidity has community-acquired pneumonia. He is alert, RR 18/min, BP 122/78 mmHg, BUN 15 mg/dL and creatinine 0.87 mg/dL. What is the most appropriate management?
items.a: Outpatient treatment with high-dose oral amoxicillin

new_themes.theme: Fanconi syndrome

items.q: A patient has glucosuria with normal blood glucose, phosphaturia, aminoaciduria and normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. What is the diagnosis?
items.a: Fanconi syndrome (generalised proximal tubular dysfunction)

new_themes.theme: UTI: เดาเชื้อจาก gram stain / สายสวน

items.q: A man with three urinary tract infections in 1 year has nitrite 1+ and a Gram stain showing gram-negative bacilli. Which organism is most likely?
items.a: Escherichia coli

items.q: A patient with a long-term indwelling urinary catheter has a urinary tract infection with gram-positive cocci in chains. Which organism is most likely?
items.a: Enterococcus faecalis

new_themes.theme: UTI ซ้ำในผู้ชาย → ตรวจต่อมลูกหมาก

items.q: An elderly man with recurrent urinary tract infections and perineal discomfort should have which examination?
items.a: Digital rectal examination to assess the prostate, with post-void residual measurement

new_themes.theme: Secondary prevention หลัง MI

items.q: After reperfusion, which combination is standard long-term secondary prevention following myocardial infarction?
items.a: Dual antiplatelet therapy, high-intensity statin, beta-blocker and ACE inhibitor with risk-factor control

new_themes.theme: Re-expansion pulmonary edema

items.q: A large pleural effusion is drained and 2 litres of fluid are removed in a single session. Shortly afterwards the patient develops cough, chest tightness and worsening hypoxaemia, with new unilateral infiltrates on the side that was drained. What is the most likely complication?
items.a: Re-expansion pulmonary oedema

new_themes.theme: Purple urine bag syndrome

items.q: A bedridden patient with a long-term catheter has purple discolouration of the urine bag. What is the cause?
items.a: Purple urine bag syndrome from bacterial indoxyl sulfate metabolism in alkaline urine

new_themes.theme: Renal TB (sterile pyuria)

items.q: A patient with sterile pyuria and chronic urinary symptoms from a TB-endemic area should have which investigation?
items.a: Urine for acid-fast bacilli and molecular testing (Xpert MTB/RIF) on early morning samples

new_themes.theme: Contrast-associated AKI

items.q: A patient with CKD needs a contrast CT. What is the best evidence-based prophylaxis against contrast-associated acute kidney injury?
items.a: Intravenous isotonic saline before and after the scan with the lowest possible contrast dose and withholding nephrotoxic drugs
